edbDesc: An outward force associated with rotation. Centrifugal force is one of several so-called pseudo-forces (or inertial forces), so named because, unlike real forces, they do not originate in interactions with other bodies situated in the environment of the particle upon which they act. Instead, centrifugal force originates in the rotation of the frame of reference within which observations are made.
title: Centrifugal force
description: Anything going round in a circle seems flung outward, pressing harder the faster it spins: water stays in a bucket swung overhead. Christiaan Huygens worked out its size in 1659. Spin it fast enough and it squeezes water from clothes, cream from milk and heavy particles from light ones.
effect: a spinning object presses outward, harder the faster it spins
strength: A washing machine spinning at 1,200 rpm presses the clothes against the drum with about 400 times their weight.
pickWhy: A clear effect with big jobs (separating, drying) that the deck lacks as a phenomenon; the Ultracentrifuge card is one invention using it.
